groups.statement: Users shall be able to load their biological datasets without friction.
Users shall be able to see the data clearly in 3D.
Users shall be able to interact with the data in a way that helps them understand patterns or specific points of interest.
For researchers and investigators, the application shall make it easy to inspect data points and retrieve the associated information accurately and quickly.
For demonstrators, the application shall present the data in a visually clear and responsive way so they can explain or show the dataset effectively during presentations.
The system shall validate the loaded dataset and render it in the 3D grid view.
The system shall allow users to select one point or multiple points.
The system shall display related metadata or results for selected points.
The grid shall support smooth rotation.
The grid shall support panning or moving.
The grid shall support zooming.
The system shall update selected-point information appropriately as users navigate the grid.
The input must include the grid data itself, identifiers, and the associated biological attributes for each point.
The input must be structured so that the application can map it unambiguously into 3D.
The system shall assume that datasets can become fairly large.
The system shall not enforce a hard record count or file size target because none has been agreed yet.
The system shall make loading and first render feel reasonable.
The system shall keep rotation responsive even with dense data.
The system shall keep zooming responsive even with dense data.
The system shall keep selecting points responsive even with dense data.
The system shall handle datasets that are too large to render all at once gracefully.
The system shall support progressive loading or a simplified display when a dataset is too large to render all at once.
The exact dataset limits still need to be confirmed.
Selected points shall stay active when the user rotates, pans, or zooms the grid.
The associated metadata for a selected point shall stay visible in a pinned or inspection panel.
The selection for a point shall persist in the background if the point is no longer visible.
The system shall make it easy to re-center or jump back to a selected point that is no longer visible.
The application shall support at least two modes.
The analytical mode shall emphasize precise inspection.
The analytical mode shall support point selection.
The analytical mode shall provide access to detailed metadata.
The analytical mode shall minimize distractions.
The demonstration mode shall prioritize clarity and presentation.
The demonstration mode shall emphasize smooth visuals.
The demonstration mode shall support easier navigation.
The demonstration mode shall support more guided or simplified interactions.
The demonstration mode shall constrain anything that could make the display confusing during a live walkthrough.
The system shall support multiple point selections by allowing users to add points one at a time or drag-select a region when practical for the grid layout.
The system shall present shared or individual metadata in a way that makes comparison straightforward.
The system shall provide a side panel or table view for comparing selected points’ metadata.
The practicality of drag-selecting a region in the 3D grid should depend mostly on dataset density.
The practicality of drag-selecting a region in the 3D grid should depend on the current zoom level.
The practicality of drag-selecting a region in the 3D grid should depend on how crowded or occluded the grid is.
When the user is zoomed far out or the points overlap heavily, region selection should be adapted to select by projected screen area rather than by a strict 3D box.
When region selection would be too ambiguous, it should be disabled.
In a sparse grid, region selection should work more directly.
In dense views, the interaction should switch to a safer, clearer selection behavior.
The application shall keep selection available in dense, zoomed-out, or heavily occluded cases rather than disabling selection entirely.
The system shall enforce basic data validation so that the grid only loads complete and structurally valid datasets.
Metadata visibility shall follow access rules.
The application shall support export and sharing capability.
The exact export formats shall depend on the formats already used by the teams.
Sharing shall respect access controls.
The Grid 3D application shall be available in a web-based form first.
The Grid 3D application may include a desktop option later if performance or specialized hardware becomes an issue.
The main deployment shall fit the lab and collaboration environment.
Specific browser or system constraints need to be confirmed.
